title: Mardi Gras as a child and the Indians
summary: Watching Rex, Zulu and the Mardi Gras Indians pass in his neighborhood and masking as a clown.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: How much, what, I'm looking at, was Mardi Gras Day a big day for you? Yeah. For your family when you were growing up or for you?

Yeah, well for me as a kid it was a great day because we used to go to, my daddy used to bring me to the old bayou just before you get to the train station that used to be. I forgot what it was, I was a child. That's where the floats used to come out on Galleup Street and they used to come through that little bayou there. I can remember that. And where I lived at all, well the wrecks would always come up Felicity Street, just come up, Claybone, Felicity to St. Charles. And all the Indians would pass and the Zulus with their time were in a limited area but they would pass right up at Great Trugate, Jackson Street and everything passed on St. Andrea and Magnolia. Right. So I mean it was a big day and everybody had a big pot of food and it was just big fun. Even as a kid I masked a few times. Where'd your mask at? Just as a clown, not as an Indian or anything but it was just fun.
Did you know the Indians? Oh yeah.

And all in the neighborhood. Different guys. Remember when you were? And they were Chilch and Wow Magnolia. Wow Magnolia. Yeah. Chief Fletcher, Bozo, Clarence Davis, all these, Big Bob. This was a big thing. I'm sorry I'm stuck for names. I know. All I'm like the guys would be making the uniforms and come by my mom and she would help. It was like everything happened. In the neighborhood. On Magnolia. Everything passed at one time. That was just another part of the city. But all you'd do was stand right there. Like I said you'd see Rex passed, you'd see Zulu passed, you'd see the Indians. And a lot of people were masked and they'd see the baby dolls and the chicks used to, it's a lot of funny things. You would fall out laughing just seeing the people don't mask as much as they used to. But I mean in the neighborhoods people would mask. And it was big fun. And it was pretty safe. I guess it was wild then but it was safe. You know you leave your door unlocked and come back. Nobody mess with your stuff, that type of thing. But I enjoyed it. Some people say, Geraldine, you were never a child. I say, yeah, because I've been playing music most of my life. I say, yeah, but I enjoyed it all. I had a chance to play with a lot of friends. We were still around. And we can reminisce about a lot of things. And we still do.
